productionFlow.root: AccessHostServices.CreateDevTunnelIdentityRoute(RepositorySource,useKind) now creates a genuine Management route for named anonymous sources too, using the same host OAuth registry and real broker graph. Explicit anonymous Web endpoints still return no route and require no discovery.
productionFlow.consumers: EntityRepository.CreateDevTunnelNameDataAccessLayerAsync and AgentPersistenceStoreSourceFactory.CreateDevTunnelAsync independently construct a named Management identity request for anonymous relay sources. Both pass the exact existing broker and live presentation callback through DevTunnelServiceFactory.
productionFlow.identity: CreateNamedManagementIdentityRequest uses a resource-bound lineage and distinct management-discovery requestor/use fingerprint. Existing route rebinding logic is reused, retaining configured GitHub/Entra/OAuth credentials and their account pins. Null/default GitHub requests remain genuinely unbound; the actual provider must supply and verify the real account.
productionFlow.management: DevTunnelServiceFactory uses its existing typed identityRequest when selecting the new internal DevTunnelNamedAnonymousEndpointResolver for anonymous name-only descriptors. The actual SDK ListTunnels call passes through the existing DevTunnelManagementAuthenticationHandler and production DevTunnelIdentityCredentialAccessExecutor. Exported identity and underlying provider release must be separately authorized before acquisition/send. Identity is borrowed only within the existing generation/policy-guarded lease callback at validated HTTPS Management destinations.
productionFlow.discovery: Read-only Management listing requests IncludePorts and the Workspaces marker, never Connect token scopes. Exactly one marker/name match is required; auto selects the unique marker-bearing tunnel. Require exactly one nonzero typed port and reuse the existing safe endpoint validator from DevTunnelConnectManagementApi. Its only change is private-to-internal helper visibility; its algorithm is unchanged.
productionFlow.relay: After discovery and Management cleanup, each consumer rebuilds its anonymous Connect request around the exact discovered endpoint, preserving the anonymous route and null account. This rebuild also recomputes the canonical logical credential identity for the endpoint. Actual relay sends remain independently broker-authorized via the existing canonical anonymous executor and DevTunnelAuthenticationHandler; no Connect mint or identity inspection is invoked for anonymous relay.
productionFlow.separation: Management identity never enters the relay request. Both Authorization and X-Tunnel-Authorization are absent at anonymous relay transport. Management never receives X-Tunnel-Authorization. Unsafe SDK redirects to relay are rejected before forwarding identity.
productionFlow.lifetime: Each discovery owns its SDK client, authentication pipeline, transport, and actual HTTP responses. A narrowly scoped response lifetime below the authentication handler drains SDK responses and sanitized request metadata because the SDK otherwise leaves successful/late response content undisposed. Existing identity leases, exact-generation replay guards and bounded retry behavior remain unchanged. Caller cancellation and broker shutdown discard late results before endpoint/relay publication.
productionFlow.errors: Discovery mismatches remain typed IdentityMismatch. Transport/SDK malformed-response failures are sanitized to ProviderFailure without original transport text/inner exception. OperationCanceledException remains cancellation; no retry loops or sleeps were added.
